name: Psychological Horror
definition: Fear grows through unstable interpretation, intrusive memory, isolation, or compromised identity while concrete consequences prevent uncertainty from becoming arbitrary.
negative_signals: fully visible creature as the only threat
ordinary internal conflict without sustained dread
diagnostic_questions: Can the reader track why more than one interpretation remains plausible?

neighbors.distinction: Psychological horror centers compromised interpretation rather than inherited place.
The threat may be real, but perception and identity remain the primary arena.

reader_promises.name: Unstable meaning
reader_promises.description: Make recurring details support multiple consequential interpretations before clarification.

reader_promises.name: Intimate dread
reader_promises.description: Tie fear to identity, memory, guilt, dependency, or loss of self-trust.

roles.name: Compromised perceiver
roles.description: Must act despite incomplete confidence in memory, senses, or motives.

roles.name: Reality anchor
roles.description: Offers verification, manipulation, or a competing account of events.

roles.name: Pressure source
roles.description: Intensifies uncertainty through a person, environment, condition, or phenomenon.

stakes: Ability to distinguish action from compulsion

movements.name: Disquiet
movements.description: Introduce a small contradiction connected to a personal vulnerability.

movements.name: Pattern formation
movements.description: Accumulate evidence that supports both threat and self-doubt.

movements.name: Interpretive isolation
movements.description: Make seeking proof damage trust or deepen exposure.

movements.name: Choice under uncertainty
movements.description: Force consequential action without granting perfect certainty.

complications.name: Ambiguous proof
complications.description: Evidence verifies an event but not the protagonist's explanation.

complications.name: Anchor fails
complications.description: The trusted verifier is mistaken, compromised, or unable to help.

complications.name: Self-caused consequence
complications.description: A protective or testing behavior creates the danger it sought to prevent.

twists.name: Both frames partly true
twists.description: Psychological vulnerability and external threat interact without reducing either to a trick.

twists.name: Anchor dependent
twists.description: The apparent stabilizer relies on the protagonist's uncertainty for identity or control.

conclusions.name: Grounded action
conclusions.description: The protagonist acts on sufficient evidence while accepting remaining uncertainty.

conclusions.name: Identity loss
conclusions.description: The pressure source absorbs or replaces the protagonist's stable self-concept.

conclusions.name: New interpretation
conclusions.description: The same facts become livable through a changed relationship to memory or fear.

subversions: Confirm an external danger without portraying vulnerability as weakness.
Let asking for help become the bravest and most effective act.
cliches_to_avoid: A diagnosis used as a surprise monster
Random contradictions that cannot be reinterpreted coherently
quality_checks: Ambiguity changes choices and has observable consequences.
Competing interpretations remain grounded in shown evidence.
The conclusion resolves agency even if ontology remains uncertain.

sources.title: The Cambridge Companion to Popular Fiction
sources.contribution: Describes bodily horror and suspense as flexible narrative pleasures that combine with character concerns.

sources.title: Aphorisms for Writing Science Fiction
sources.author_or_organization: Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association
sources.contribution: Supports action grounded in character imperatives, thematic structure, and economical payoff.
